Run QA on issue #1063 and PR #1064 in the wp-media/imagify-plugin repository.

Working directory: /Users/gaelrobin/Local Sites/imagify/app/public/wp-content/plugins/imagify-plugin

## Issue summary
**#1063 — WP 7.0 - Icon shifted with text in button**

WordPress 7.0 introduced a new CSS rule:
```css
.wp-core-ui .button .dashicons,
.wp-core-ui .button-primary .dashicons,
.wp-core-ui .button-secondary .dashicons {
    line-height: 1.9;
    vertical-align: top;
}
```
This caused dashicons inside Imagify buttons to shift upward, misaligning with the button label text.

## What was changed (PR #1064)
Only `assets/css/admin.css` and `assets/css/admin.min.css` were modified. Two CSS rule-sets had `line-height: 1` added:

1. `[class*="imagify-"] .button .dashicons` — now has `margin-right:5px; vertical-align:middle; line-height:1`
2. `.imagify-settings .button .dashicons, .imagify-welcome .button .dashicons, .imagify-notice .button .dashicons, .imagify-button.imagify-button .dashicons, .imagify-button-primary.imagify-button-primary .dashicons, .imagify-button-secondary.imagify-button-secondary .dashicons` — now has `vertical-align:middle; line-height:1`

## Acceptance criteria
- Dashicons inside Imagify buttons are vertically aligned with button label text.
- No visual regression on the Settings page, Bulk Optimization page, or Media Library.

## Environment
- wp-env is running on http://localhost:8888 (confirmed reachable).
- Branch: fix/1063-wp-7-0-icon
- PR: https://github.com/wp-media/imagify-plugin/pull/1064

## Your tasks
1. Select appropriate QA strategies based on the change type (CSS/UI only — no PHP/JS changed).
2. Since this is a UI change, delegate browser testing to the e2e-qa-tester sub-agent. Have it:
   - Open the Imagify Settings page and inspect buttons with dashicons.
   - Take screenshots of buttons to confirm icon alignment.
   - Check the Bulk Optimization page as well.
   - Write or update a Playwright spec under Tests/e2e/specs/ that verifies the CSS property is applied correctly (or visually smoke-tests the pages).
   - Run `bash bin/test-e2e.sh` to confirm the suite is green.
   - Commit any new/updated test files to the branch and push.
3. Post the full QA report as a comment on PR #1064.
4. Return a structured report: READY TO MERGE / PARTIAL / FAIL with details.

{"baseRefName":"chore/add-ai-assistant","body":"# Description

Fixes #1063

WordPress 7.0 introduced a new CSS rule that sets `line-height: 1.9` and `vertical-align: top` on `.dashicons` elements inside WP core button classes (`.button`, `.button-primary`, `.button-secondary`) within `.wp-core-ui`. This caused Imagify's button icons to shift upward, misaligning them with their label text.

The fix adds `line-height: 1` to the existing Imagify button dashicon selectors in `admin.css`, which neutralises WP 7.0's new rule and restores correct icon–text alignment across all Imagify pages (Settings, Welcome, Notices, and custom Imagify button components).

## Type of change

- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality).
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue).
- [ ] Enhancement (non-breaking change which improves an existing functionality).
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as before).
- [ ] Sub-task of #1063
- [ ] Chore
- [ ] Release

## Detailed scenario

### What was tested

- Opened Imagify Settings, Bulk Optimization, and Media Library pages under WordPress 7.0.
- Verified that all buttons containing a dashicon (e.g. "Check API key", "Add folder", "Optimize") display the icon correctly aligned with the label text.
- Verified no visual regression on WordPress 6.x (the `line-height: 1` value matches the pre-7.0 default, so it is a no-op there).

### How to test

1. Install or update to WordPress 7.0.
2. Activate the Imagify plugin.
3. Navigate to **Settings → Imagify** and inspect the buttons that contain dashicons (e.g. "Check API key" button with the refresh icon).
4. Confirm the icon is vertically centred with the button label — no upward shift.
5. Navigate to **Media → Bulk Optimization** and check any dashicon-bearing buttons there as well.
6. As a regression check, repeat on WordPress 6.7 to confirm icons are still properly aligned.

### Affected Features & Quality Assurance Scope

- Imagify Settings page (all buttons with dashicons)
- Imagify Welcome/onboarding screen
- Imagify admin notices that contain buttons
- Any `.imagify-button-primary` / `.imagify-button-secondary` component with a dashicon child

No PHP logic, no JavaScript, no REST endpoints are changed.

## Technical description

### Documentation

WordPress 7.0 ships with the following addition to its core `buttons.css`:

```css
.wp-core-ui .button .dashicons,
.wp-core-ui .button-primary .dashicons,
.wp-core-ui .button-secondary .dashicons {
    line-height: 1.9;
    vertical-align: top;
}
```

Imagify already overrode `vertical-align` back to `middle` through two selectors in `admin.css`:

```css
[class*="imagify-"] .button .dashicons { vertical-align: middle; }

.imagify-settings .button .dashicons,
.imagify-welcome .button .dashicons,
.imagify-notice .button .dashicons,
.imagify-button.imagify-button .dashicons,
.imagify-button-primary.imagify-button-primary .dashicons,
.imagify-button-secondary.imagify-button-secondary .dashicons { vertical-align: middle; }
```

Both selectors have the same specificity (0,3,0) as the WP 7.0 rule, and Imagify's stylesheet is enqueued after core, so `vertical-align: middle` was already winning — but `line-height` was never set, so the inherited `1.9` was expanding the line-box and shifting icons upward.

Adding `line-height: 1` to both existing rule-sets is the minimal targeted fix.

### New dependencies

None.

### Risks

Low. Only two CSS declarations are added, scoped to Imagify's own button selectors. The value `line-height: 1` matches the browser default for icon-font elements and has no effect on older WordPress versions.

# Imagify — End-to-End Testing

This document is the canonical reference for the Imagify Playwright E2E test suite. **Read this before writing any new tests.**

---

## Architecture overview

| Layer | Path | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| Config | `Tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts` | Playwright base config (baseURL, reporters, timeouts) |
| Fixtures | `Tests/e2e/fixtures/` | Shared helpers: login, WP-CLI wrapper, API key guard |
| Page objects | `Tests/e2e/pages/` | One class per major admin surface |
| Specs | `Tests/e2e/specs/` | Test files, one per feature area |
| Dev scripts | `bin/dev-up.sh`, `bin/dev-down.sh`, `bin/dev-seed.sh` | Local environment lifecycle |
| CI | `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` | Automated runs on pull requests |


All tests run against a local WordPress environment managed by `@wordpress/env` (Docker). The environment maps the plugin root directly into the container at `wp-content/plugins/imagify`.

---

## Admin URLs

| Surface | URL |
|---------|-----|
| Settings | `/wp-admin/options-general.php?page=imagify` |
| Bulk optimization | `/wp-admin/upload.php?page=imagify-bulk-optimization` |
| Custom folders | `/wp-admin/upload.php?page=imagify-files` |
| Media library (list) | `/wp-admin/upload.php?mode=list` |
| Plugins list | `/wp-admin/plugins.php` |

---

## Running tests locally

### One-time setup

```bash
# From the repository root
bash bin/dev-up.sh       # Start wp-env + activate plugin + seed test data
cd Tests/e2e
npm install
npx playwright install chromium
```

### Running

```bash
cd Tests/e2e
npm test                 # Headless, list reporter
npm run test:headed      # With browser UI visible
npm run test:ui          # Playwright interactive UI mode
npm run report           # Open the last HTML report
```

### Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `IMAGIFY_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8888` | Override the WordPress base URL |
| `IMAGIFY_ADMIN_USER` | `admin` | WP admin username |
| `IMAGIFY_ADMIN_PASS` | `password` | WP admin password |
| `IMAGIFY_TESTS_API_KEY` | _(unset)_ | Real Imagify API key — required for optimization tests |

Set `IMAGIFY_TESTS_API_KEY` to run tests that call the Imagify API. Without it, those tests are automatically skipped.

---

## Page objects

Each major admin surface has a Page Object class. Use them instead of raw selectors — they centralize selector maintenance.

### `SettingsPage` (`Tests/e2e/pages/settings.ts`)

```typescript
import { SettingsPage } from '../pages/settings';
const settings = new SettingsPage( page );
await settings.goto();
await settings.setApiKey( process.env.IMAGIFY_TESTS_API_KEY! );
```

Key members: `apiKeyInput`, `saveButton`, `successNotice`, `goto()`, `setApiKey()`, `getApiKey()`, `expectNoFatalError()`.

### `BulkOptimizationPage` (`Tests/e2e/pages/bulk-optimization.ts`)

```typescript
import { BulkOptimizationPage } from '../pages/bulk-optimization';
const bulk = new BulkOptimizationPage( page );
await bulk.goto();
await expect( bulk.optimizeButton ).toBeVisible();
```

Key members: `optimizeButton`, `progressBar`, `statsTable`, `goto()`, `expectNoFatalError()`.

### `MediaLibraryPage` (`Tests/e2e/pages/media-library.ts`)

```typescript
import { MediaLibraryPage } from '../pages/media-library';
const library = new MediaLibraryPage( page );
